extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: MATHVISTA is a benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks. It consists of 6,141 examples, derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection involved gathering 9 existing MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets containing math-related instances. For the VQA datasets, heuristic rules and manual labeling were used to filter relevant examples. Additionally, three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) were created and manually annotated by STEM graduate students.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of 28 existing multimodal datasets (MathQA and VQA) and newly sourced visual contexts including puzzle test figures from online learning platforms, functional plots, and academic illustrations (tables, figures, charts) from papers on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were trained using detailed instructions and examples to classify problems. The process involved independent annotation by multiple reviewers, followed by a review phase where any discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire team to reach a consensus.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom developed annotation tool with a GUI
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement was measured using consistency rates and the Fleiss Kappa score, achieving a 99.2% consistency rate for new datasets and a Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775 for mathematical reasoning labeling.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields and expert annotators
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has limitations in coverage, potentially missing certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. Scalability and generalizability to other domains are concerns. Additionally, only 85.6% of examples have annotations, and due to heterogeneous sources, these annotations lack a unified format and structure.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended to be used as a benchmark to facilitate the development of mathematical reasoning systems in visual contexts and to evaluate the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Large Multimodal Models (LMMs).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors are committed to maintaining the dataset as an ongoing research process. They plan to refine potential data noise based on community feedback, evolve the leaderboard for new models, and release future iterations with broader problem coverage and unified annotations.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: A sampling strategy was used to create the testmini subset, ensuring representation from each source dataset by first randomly sampling a threshold of 4 questions per source, then proportionally sampling the rest.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Quality checks were performed to identify and address errors in the data.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: One limitation is the dataset coverage. While MATHVISTA encompasses a broad spectrum of tasks and visual contexts, there may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. [...] Thus, the scalability and generalizability of our benchmark to other domains remain a concern. Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples (Table 1) having annotations. Due to the heterogeneity of these sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: Therefore, it is essential to develop a new benchmark to (1) facilitate the development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios, and (2) evaluate the research progress of LLMs and LMMs, especially their capabilities in solving rigorous reasoning tasks.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: In future iterations, our benchmark will be beneficial to encompass a broader array of problems and visual contexts, while also providing unified and comprehensive annotations. Our benchmark is part of an ongoing research process, and we are committed to maintaining the datasets, such as refining the potential data noise, in response to the community feedback. Also, we are committed to evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: we adopted this sampling strategy: (1) first, randomly sample questions with a threshold number of 4 for each source dataset; (2) then, randomly sample the remaining questions for each source dataset on its proportion in the entire set.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We also conducted several quality checks to address any unidentified errors.
